mainTopic: The source for עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה, and רב's rulings on an אבל (תפילין, סוכה) and the wedding party's exemptions
overview: This amud finishes the search for a source for עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה (someone busy with one מצוה is exempt from another). The question is who the טמאים were who could not bring the קרבן פסח. רבי עקיבא says they were מישאל and אלצפן. רבי יצחק rejects this, and he concludes they were people burying a מת מצוה whose seventh day fell on ערב פסח. A צריכא then explains why both sources (the חתן with קריאת שמע and the טמאים with פסח) are needed. Next, with גופא, the גמרא turns to rulings of רבי אבא בר זבדא in the name of רב. An אבל is exempt from תפילין only on the first day of mourning. He is still obligated in סוכה, because his sadness does not come from the סוכה. The wedding party is exempt from סוכה for all seven days, because their joy and their meal belong in the חופה. אביי and רבא give different reasons why the חופה cannot simply be put in the סוכה. רבי זירא tells how he chose to eat in the סוכה and rejoice in the חופה anyway. The amud ends with a ברייתא: the wedding party is exempt from תפלה and תפילין but must say קריאת שמע.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא identifies the impure men as מישאל and אלצפן
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the טמאים who missed the פסח were מישאל and אלצפן, who carried out the bodies of נדב ואביהוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: They were מישאל and אלצפן, who were busy taking care of נדב and אביהוא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the debate over who the טמאים were who could not bring the קרבן פסח. רבי עקיבא gives his answer: מישאל and אלצפן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה tells us that מישאל and אלצפן carried out the bodies of נדב ואביהוא, which made them טמא מת. רבי עקיבא suggests that this is why they could not bring the פסח. This is the second identification, after the earlier view of the bearers of יוסף's coffin.

keyTerms.meaning: אהרן's cousins, who carried out the bodies of נדב ואביהוא (ויקרא י:ד)
אהרן's sons, who died when they brought a foreign fire

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
They were Mishael and Elzaphan,
phrases.notes: "They" are the impure men in במדבר ט who couldn't bring the פסח.

phrases.english: who were busy with (the bodies of) Nadav and Avihu.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier debate on the דף (after רבי יוסי הגלילי's view of the bearers of יוסף's coffin), offering a second identification.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The טמאים were מישאל and אלצפן, made טמא by carrying נדב ואביהוא.

steps.title: רבי יצחק objects that both groups could already have become pure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק argues that both the bearers of יוסף's coffin and מישאל ואלצפן had enough time to become טהור before פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: If they were the people carrying יוסף's coffin, they could already have become pure. If they were מישאל and אלצפן, they could have become pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק attacks both earlier identifications. Each group had more than seven days before ערב פסח, so they could have finished their טהרה in time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאת מת lasts seven days. The bearers of יוסף's coffin had been carrying it for a long time and had camped at סיני long enough to become pure. נדב ואביהוא died on ראש חודש ניסן, which leaves more than seven days before the fourteenth. So neither group fits a story about people who were still טמא on ערב פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: those carrying יוסף's coffin out of מצרים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם נוֹשְׂאֵי אֲרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף הָיוּ,
phrases.english: If they were the bearers of Joseph's coffin,
phrases.notes: This argues against the first opinion, that of רבי יוסי הגלילי, from earlier on the דף.

phrases.english: they could already have become pure.
If they were Mishael and Elzaphan,
they could have become pure.
phrases.notes: נדב ואביהוא died on א׳ ניסן, which is more than seven days before י״ד ניסן

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק אוֹמֵר: אִם נוֹשְׂאֵי אֲרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's identification and the earlier one together.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both identifications of the טמאים (the bearers of יוסף's coffin, and מישאל ואלצפן)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A seven-day טומאה would have ended before ערב פסח in both cases, so neither group would have been unable to bring the פסח.

steps.title: Rabbi Yitzchak's alternative: they were busy with a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק concludes that they were unnamed people who buried a מת מצוה, and their seventh day of טומאה fell exactly on ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they were busy with a מת מצוה, and their seventh day fell on ערב פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting both earlier answers, רבי יצחק gives his own. These were people who buried a מת מצוה, and their seventh day landed right on ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His timing fixes the problem from the previous step: they really were still טמא when the פסח was slaughtered. Because they were busy with a מצוה (burying the dead), they were exempt from the פסח. This keeps the case as a source for עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: a corpse with no one else to bury it, so anyone who finds it must bury it
the 14th of ניסן, when the קרבן פסח is slaughtered

phrases.english: Rather, they were busy with a מצוה-corpse (an abandoned body)
whose seventh day (of impurity) fell
to be on the eve of Pesach,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the two identifications rejected in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement identification that fits the timing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טמאים were a known group (the bearers of יוסף's coffin, or מישאל ואלצפן).
steps.terutzMaskana: They were people who buried a מת מצוה, and their seventh day was ערב פסח itself.

steps.title: Proof from the verse that the next day they could bring the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says they could not bring the פסח "on that day." This implies that the next day they could, so their seventh day was ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "And they could not bring the פסח on that day." On that day they could not, which means that the next day they could!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק proves his timing from the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "on that day" limit the problem to that one day. This means their טהרה would be complete by the next day. So the day of the slaughter had to be their seventh day, when they could not yet bring a קרבן but would become טהור at nightfall.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְלֹא יָכְלוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת הַפֶּסַח בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא״,
phrases.english: As it says: "And they could not bring the Pesach on that day" (Bamidbar 9:6),
on that day they cannot bring it,
which implies that the next day they can bring it!

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְלֹא יָכְלוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת הַפֶּסַח בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the timing claimed in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That their seventh day fell on ערב פסח
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר ט:ו, "בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא" implies they could on the next day
steps.whatToRemember: The טמאים who missed the פסח were busy with a מת מצוה, and their seventh day fell on ערב פסח. Their exemption from the פסח is a source for עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה.

steps.title: Why the פסח source alone would not teach the חתן case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that both sources are needed. From פסח alone we might think the exemption works only because the פסח's time had not yet come when they began the burial. With a חתן, the time for קריאת שמע has already arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If we only had the case there (פסח), I would say it works because the time of the פסח obligation had not yet arrived. But here, where the time of שמע has arrived, I would say no. So it is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the unstated question of why we need two sources (the חתן with קריאת שמע and the טמאים with פסח) for the same rule. This step shows what the פסח case alone would fail to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טמאים took on the burial before the פסח obligation had started, so we could think they were simply allowed to finish what they began first. A חתן, though, is busy at a time when קריאת שמע is already due. So we need the חתן source to teach that he is exempt even then.

keyTerms.meaning: it is necessary (both sources are needed)

steps.confusionAlert: In this צריכא, "הָתָם" (there) means the פסח / טמאים case, and "הָכָא" (here) means the חתן and קריאת שמע case. These meanings stay the same in the next step. Only the order is reversed: the next step starts from הָכָא (שמע) and then asks about הָתָם (פסח).

phrases.english: It is necessary, for if it had taught us only there (the Pesach case),

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא מְטָא זְמַן חִיּוּבָא דְּפֶסַח,
phrases.english: (I would say the exemption is) because the time of the Pesach obligation had not yet arrived,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דִּמְטָא זְמַן קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע —
phrases.english: but here, where the time of Shema has arrived,
I would say no (no exemption). So it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the פסח source now settled, the גמרא justifies keeping both it and the חתן source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסח case alone could be limited to a situation where the second מצוה had not yet become due. The חתן case shows the exemption applies even when it already has.

steps.title: Why the שמע source alone would not teach the פסח case
steps.stepSummary: From the חתן case alone we might think the exemption applies only to קריאת שמע, which carries no כרת. We would not apply it to פסח, which does carry כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had taught us only here (שמע), I would say it is because there is no כרת. But there (פסח), where there is כרת, I would say no. So it is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the צריכא. It shows what the חתן case alone would fail to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Skipping קריאת שמע carries no כרת, so an exemption there is easy to accept. Missing the פסח carries כרת, so we might think a person must not skip it even while busy with another מצוה. The פסח source teaches that the exemption holds even for a מצוה with כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: spiritual cutting-off, the punishment for skipping the קרבן פסח on purpose

steps.whatToRemember: Both sources are needed. The פסח case shows the exemption works even for a severe מצוה with כרת. The חתן case shows it works even when the second מצוה's time has already arrived.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only here (Shema),
(I would say it is) because there is no karet,
but there (Pesach), where there is karet,
I would say no. So it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-way צריכא begun in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חתן case alone could be limited to a light מצוה without כרת. The פסח case extends the exemption to a severe מצוה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Neither source is extra. Each one blocks a different way of limiting the rule of עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה.

steps.title: רב's rule: a mourner is exempt only from תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic with גופא. It quotes רב's rule that an אבל is obligated in every מצוה except תפילין, because תפילין are called פאר (splendor).
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself: רבי אבא בר זבדא said in the name of רב: A mourner is obligated in all the מצוות stated in the תורה except תפילין, because they are called "splendor."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now returns to a statement it quoted earlier only in passing, and examines it on its own. רב says an אבל keeps all מצוות except תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a mourner does not exempt a person from מצוות in general. The one exception is תפילין, because the פסוק calls them פאר (an ornament), and wearing an ornament does not fit mourning. The source for calling תפילין פאר comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: "the matter itself": returning to examine a statement quoted earlier
splendor, an ornament (a name for תפילין)

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said in the name of Rav:
A mourner is obligated in all the מצוות
stated in the Torah, except for tefillin,
for the term "splendor" is said about them.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section. It goes back to a statement mentioned earlier on the דף and analyzes it directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל is obligated in all מצוות except תפילין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the halacha that an אבל does not put on תפילין on the first day of mourning.

steps.title: Proof from יחזקאל: only he had to wear תפילין while mourning
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ specially commanded יחזקאל to "bind your splendor upon you" while mourning. This shows that other mourners are exempt from תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Merciful One told יחזקאל, "Bind your splendor upon you," it means: you are obligated, but everyone else is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רב learned that an אבל is exempt from תפילין. The proof is the special command to יחזקאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יחזקאל was told not to mourn his wife in the usual way. Part of that instruction was to wear his פאר (תפילין). A special instruction for him alone implies that normal mourners do not wear תפילין. So other אבלים are exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: An אבל is exempt from תפילין. We learn this from the fact that יחזקאל needed a special command to wear his פאר while mourning.

phrases.english: Since the Merciful One said to Ezekiel
"Bind your splendor upon you, etc." (Yechezkel 24:17),
it is you who are obligated,
but everyone else is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the תפילין exception in רב's rule.
steps.raayaObject: That an אבל is exempt from תפילין
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל כד:יז, a special command to יחזקאל implies that others are exempt

steps.title: The תפילין exemption is only on the first day
steps.stepSummary: The אבל is exempt from תפילין only on the first day of mourning. A פסוק in עמוס teaches that the main bitterness lasts one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only on the first day, as it is written: 'and its end like a bitter day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רב's rule from the previous step. The אבל is exempt from תפילין only on the first day of mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'a bitter day' in the singular. This teaches that the sharpest stage of mourning lasts one day. After that day, the אבל puts on תפילין again.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only to... (a limiting formula)

steps.whatToRemember: An אבל skips תפילין only on day one of mourning.

phrases.english: And this applies only on the first day,
as it is written: 'and its end like a bitter day.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the תפילין exemption that steps 7-8 proved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אבל's exemption from תפילין applies only on the first day.

steps.title: A mourner must sit in the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר זבדא quotes רב: an אבל is obligated in סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבא בר זבדא said in the name of רב: A mourner is obligated in סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of רב. A mourner is still required to sit in the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another rule about an אבל and a מצוה. Unlike תפילין on the first day, mourning does not exempt him from סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligated in the מצוה of סוכה

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said that Rav said:
A mourner is obligated in the sukka.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling about an אבל, related in theme to רב's תפילין rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל is obligated in סוכה.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב needed to say this at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling as too obvious to need saying. This sets up the next step, which will explain why it was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אבל is obligated in every מצוה except תפילין, so of course he must sit in the סוכה. Why would רב teach something we already know?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a statement adds nothing new)

phrases.english: Is it not obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for step 10's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that an אבל is obligated in סוכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אבל is obligated in all מצוות except תפילין, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A mourner's sadness does not count as סוכה suffering
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought the אבל is a מצטער, who is exempt from סוכה. רב teaches that this exemption covers only discomfort caused by the סוכה itself. The אבל's sadness comes from himself, so he must calm his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since רב said one who is suffering is exempt from סוכה, this mourner is also suffering. So he teaches us: that rule applies to suffering that comes on its own. Here, he is the one causing himself sorrow, and he should settle his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב's ruling was needed. Without it, we might have exempted a mourner as someone who is suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a מצטער is exempt from סוכה. That rule covers discomfort that comes from the סוכה itself, such as cold, heat, or a bad smell. The mourner's sorrow does not come from the סוכה, so he is expected to settle his mind and fulfill the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said... (introduces a mistaken assumption)
One who is suffering or uncomfortable
Suffering that comes on its own (from the סוכה)

steps.confusionAlert: The מצטער exemption is not about feeling sad in general. It covers only discomfort that comes from being in the סוכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the boundary of the מצטער exemption, an important rule in הלכות סוכה.

phrases.english: Lest you say:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: since Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said that Rav said:
one who is suffering is exempt from the sukka —
this one too is suffering,
he teaches us:
that applies only to suffering that comes on its own,
but here, he is the one
who is causing himself to suffer,
he should settle his mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows a reasonable mistaken assumption that the ruling prevents
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An אבל counts as a מצטער and is exempt from סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מצטער exemption covers only discomfort caused by the סוכה. Self-generated sorrow does not exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: A mourner is not a מצטער for סוכה, because the סוכה is not causing his pain.

steps.title: The wedding party is exempt from סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the חתן, the שושבינין, and all members of the wedding party are exempt from סוכה for all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבא בר זבדא said in the name of רב: The groom, the groomsmen, and all members of the wedding party are exempt from סוכה all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ruling of רב. The groom and his wedding party are exempt from סוכה during the seven days of wedding celebration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a surprising exemption from a מצוה. The next steps will ask for the reason and test it.

keyTerms.meaning: Groomsmen, close friends who help celebrate

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said that Rav said:
The groom and the groomsmen and all members of the wedding party —
are exempt from the sukka all seven days.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling from the same chain of tradition, on a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חתן and wedding party are exempt from סוכה for all seven days.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the wedding party is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב's exemption. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the reason lets the גמרא test the exemption's limits in the steps that follow.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the wedding party is exempt from סוכה

steps.title: Because they need to rejoice
steps.stepSummary: They are exempt because they must celebrate the wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they need to rejoice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wedding party is exempt because they need to celebrate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of wedding joy is what pushes aside סוכה. The next challenges ask why that joy cannot happen in the סוכה.

phrases.english: Because they need to rejoice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14.

steps.title: Why not eat and rejoice in the סוכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: let them hold both the meal and the celebration in the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them eat in the סוכה and rejoice in the סוכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If they need to rejoice, they could do it inside the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Joy and סוכה seem able to go together. If so, the need to rejoice should not exempt them.

phrases.english: Let them eat in the sukka
and rejoice in the sukka!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that rejoicing requires exemption
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rejoicing could take place inside the סוכה.

steps.title: Wedding joy belongs in the חופה
steps.stepSummary: Wedding celebration happens only in the חופה, the newlyweds' wedding home.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no joy except in the wedding home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wedding celebration must take place in the חופה, the couple's wedding home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here חופה means the room or home where the new couple lives. The celebration belongs there, not in the סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the wedding home of the newlyweds

phrases.english: There is joy only in the wedding home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines where wedding joy must take place
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Joy can happen anywhere, including the סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wedding joy is tied to the חופה.

steps.title: Then eat in the סוכה and celebrate in the חופה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests splitting the two: eat in the סוכה, then celebrate in the חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them eat in the סוכה and rejoice in the wedding home!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. They could eat their meal in the סוכה and then go celebrate in the חופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting the meal from the celebration would satisfy both the סוכה and the wedding joy.

phrases.english: Let them eat in the sukka
and rejoice in the wedding home!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 17's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to exempt them from eating in the סוכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the celebration needs the חופה, not the meal.

steps.title: Joy goes with the meal
steps.stepSummary: Joy happens only where the meal is, so the meal must also be in the חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no joy except in the place of the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the joy and the meal cannot be split apart. The celebration happens where the meal is eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Joy must be in the חופה, and joy follows the meal. So the meal must be in the חופה too, and that is why they cannot eat in the סוכה.

phrases.english: There is joy only in the place of the meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Links the joy to the meal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The meal and the celebration can be in separate places.
steps.terutzMaskana: Joy requires the meal, so both must be in the חופה.

steps.title: Why not set up the חופה inside the סוכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: make the סוכה itself the wedding home.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them make the wedding home in the סוכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges once more. They could set up the חופה inside the סוכה and keep everything there. This sets up a debate between אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both the meal and the joy must be in the חופה, put the חופה in the סוכה. Then all needs would be met in one place.

phrases.english: And let them make the wedding home in the sukka?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the exemption after step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The exemption of the wedding party
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Combining the חופה and the סוכה would remove any need for the exemption.

steps.title: אביי: concern of ייחוד
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the חופה cannot be in the סוכה because of the problem of ייחוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Because of seclusion.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that a חופה in the סוכה could lead to ייחוד. The bride could end up alone with another man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה was often built on a roof, away from the house. If the groom stepped out, the bride might be left alone there with another man, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The ban on a woman being alone with a man who is not her husband

phrases.english: Abaye said: Because of seclusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a prohibition that would result
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חופה could be placed in the סוכה.

steps.title: רבא: the groom's discomfort
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the reason is צער חתן: the groom would lack privacy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: Because of the groom's distress.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. The groom would be distressed in a סוכה because it is open and lacks privacy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה is not fully closed off, so the couple could not have proper privacy. That distress to the groom is the reason not to put the חופה there.

phrases.english: And Rava said: Because of the distress of the groom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to step 20, differing from אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different harm: lack of privacy
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חופה could be placed in the סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The groom would lack privacy and be distressed.

steps.title: What is the difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical difference between אביי and רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks in what case אביי's and רבא's reasons would lead to different results. This sets up the final step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that the חופה should not be in the סוכה. The question is whether their reasons ever produce a different ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares steps 21 and 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where אביי and רבא would rule differently

steps.title: The case of a busy סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a סוכה where people often go in and out. For אביי there is no ייחוד concern there. For רבא the groom's lack of privacy remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is where people commonly go in and out there. According to the one who says seclusion, there is no problem. According to the one who says the groom's distress, there is a problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the case where the two reasons split: a סוכה with frequent foot traffic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When people keep coming and going, the bride will never be alone with a man, so אביי's ייחוד concern disappears. That same traffic makes privacy even worse, so רבא's concern still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
According to the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: The wedding party is exempt from סוכה because their joy and meal belong in the חופה. A חופה in the סוכה is avoided because of ייחוד (אביי) or the groom's lack of privacy (רבא). The two differ in a busy סוכה.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where people commonly go out and come in there.
According to the one who says because of seclusion — there is no concern.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם צַעַר חָתָן — אִיכָּא.
phrases.english: According to the one who says because of the groom's distress — there is a concern.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In a סוכה with frequent traffic, אביי sees no problem and רבא still sees one.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two reasons differ when people regularly enter and leave the סוכה.

steps.title: רבי זירא ate in the סוכה and celebrated in the חופה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא describes his own wedding. He ate his meals in the סוכה and did his rejoicing in the חופה, and he was doubly happy because he fulfilled two מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: I ate in the סוכה and rejoiced in the חופה (the wedding home). My heart was all the more joyful because I was doing two מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא shares a personal story to show that a חתן can manage both מצוות: eating in the סוכה and celebrating in the wedding home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 18-19, the גמרא rejected the idea of eating in the סוכה and rejoicing in the חופה, because joy belongs where the meal is. רבי זירא did exactly that split anyway, and he says his joy was even greater because he kept two מצוות. He did not make this a rule for others. A חתן stays exempt, and this was a personal choice.

keyTerms.meaning: The wedding canopy or wedding home where the couple celebrates

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not saying every חתן must eat in the סוכה. A חתן is exempt. רבי זירא is describing what he chose to do himself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
I ate in the sukka
phrases.notes: רש"י explains that he got married on ערב סוכות, so this happened during the festival.

phrases.english: and rejoiced in the wedding home,
phrases.notes: The celebrating happened in the חופה, not in the סוכה.

phrases.english: and all the more so my heart rejoiced
phrases.notes: The joy was even greater because of what follows.

phrases.english: because I was doing two [מצוות].
phrases.notes: The two are the מצוה of סוכה and the מצוה of wedding joy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: אֲנָא אֲכַלִי בַּסּוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the option rejected in steps 18-19 (eating in the סוכה and rejoicing in the חופה). רבי זירא reports that he personally chose to do this, so he kept both מצוות even though a חתן is exempt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חתן can choose to eat in the סוכה while doing his celebrating in the חופה, and so fulfill both מצוות.

steps.title: Wedding party is exempt from תפלה and תפילין but must say קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the חתן, the שושבינין, and the whole wedding party are exempt from תפלה and תפילין, but they are obligated in קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The groom, the groomsmen, and all the members of the wedding party are exempt from prayer and from תפילין, but they are obligated to recite שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that moves from סוכה to other מצוות and lists which ones the wedding party is exempt from and which one they still must do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three groups are covered here: the חתן himself, his close friends, and everyone at the wedding. They are exempt from תפלה and תפילין. Some explain this is because their great joy and lightheartedness keep them from having the proper focus. But they must still say קריאת שמע, which sets up the obvious next question: why is קריאת שמע treated differently?

keyTerms.meaning: Groomsmen, the חתן's close friends who help run the wedding

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up תְּפִלָּה (prayer) with תְּפִילִּין (phylacteries). They are spelled almost the same, but the ברייתא lists them as two separate מצוות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא widens the rule of exemption beyond the חתן to his whole wedding party. It also creates a contrast, exempt from some מצוות but not from קריאת שמע, which the גמרא will need to explain.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The groom and the groomsmen and all the members of the wedding party,
are exempt from prayer and from tefillin,
phrases.notes: That's because their joy and lightheartedness get in the way of proper focus.

phrases.english: but they are obligated in reciting Shema.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חָתָן וְהַשּׁוֹשְׁבִינִין וְכׇל בְּנֵי חוּפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the חתן's exemption from סוכה to a ברייתא about the wedding party's exemptions from other מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חתן, the שושבינין, and all בני חופה are exempt from תפלה and תפילין but obligated in קריאת שמע.
